final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced (simulated Windows). This VM runs Linux, so I didn't run it on a real Windows machine.

**Expected:** With cwd `C:\Project`, `F:\foo.js` is ignored. `ESLint` should report "File ignored because outside of base path." and `Linter#verify` should report "No matching configuration found".

**Actual:** On eslint 9.14.0 (this checkout), `F:\foo.js` gets linted by both `Linter#verify` and `ESLint#lintText`, and both report `no-undef: 'foo' is not defined.`. `ESLint#isPathIgnored("F:\\foo.js")` also returns `false`. Two controls behave correctly: `C:\Project\foo.js` is linted, and `C:\Other\foo.js` (same drive, outside cwd) is ignored with "outside of base path".

**Trigger:** The file is on a different drive from the base path (cwd). `path.win32.relative("C:\\Project", "F:\\foo.js")` returns the absolute path `"F:\\foo.js"` instead of something starting with `..`. The script prints this value for all three cases.

**Run:** `node repro/issue-18575-windows-other-drive.js`. It exits 1 and prints `BUG` lines for the different-drive case; the two controls print `OK`.

**Reliability:** Deterministic. The result is the same on every run.

**How the simulation works:** The script loads ESLint and its rules first. It then replaces the methods of the shared `node:path` module with `path.win32` and makes `process.cwd()` return `C:\Project`. I used `lintText` with a `filePath` instead of a real `F:\` file on disk, so this covers the same `ESLint` code path as `eslint --no-config-lookup F:\foo.js` except the file-system and glob steps. No production code was changed.

**Likely cause:** `@eslint/config-array` (`node_modules/@eslint/config-array/dist/cjs/index.cjs`, around lines 953–955, plus `shouldIgnorePath` and `isDirectoryIgnored`) treats a path as outside the base path only when `relativeFilePath.startsWith("..")`. On Windows, a file on another drive produces an absolute relative path, so it fails that check.

**Artifacts:** `repro/issue-18575-windows-other-drive.js` (the only change). If you want, I can confirm it on a real Windows machine with the exact CLI command from the report.
